headline: ABU DHABI'S IRH BIDS £352.8M ($462M) FOR KENMARE RESOURCES — 52% Premium for Moma Titanium Mine in Mozambique; Board Unanimously Minded to Accept
snippet: International Resources Holding (IRH), Abu Dhabi's mining investment arm under the 2PointZero Group, agreed the main financial terms for a possible cash acquisition of Kenmare Resources (Dublin, LSE: KMR) at 380 pence per share — a 52% premium to Kenmare's November 20 closing price — valuing the company at approximately £352.8 million ($462 million). Kenmare operates the Moma mine in Mozambique, one of the world's largest titanium minerals deposits, making the deal a rare major acquisition in the titanium feedstocks sector; the board has said it is unanimously minded to recommend the offer. Under Irish takeover rules, IRH must make a firm offer or walk away by 5pm Dublin time on December 15 — with up to $25 million in interim funding being negotiated to keep Kenmare operating until completion.

headline: FIREFLY METALS LANDS SECOND COPPER DISCOVERY IN ONE MONTH — Nash Returns 26.7m @ 2.3% Cu, Including 9.6m @ 4.6%; Green Bay Camp Expands
snippet: FireFly Metals (ASX: FFM) reported its second major copper discovery in a single month at the Green Bay project in Newfoundland, with the Nash discovery's first hole returning 26.7 metres at 2.3% copper from 9 metres depth, including a higher-grade zone of 9.6 metres at 4.6% copper. The discovery came from an EM conductor within 10 kilometres of the mothballed Ming mine and follows the Mount Joy discovery from late October — demonstrating that Green Bay is a genuinely active exploration camp with district-scale potential. The adjacent RDI prospect, 1.1 km along the same conductor, also returned 11.2 metres at 1.2% copper, suggesting this is not a one-hole anomaly but a widespread copper system.

headline: COPPER'S BIGGEST ONE-DAY LME DROP IN 19 MONTHS — Breaks $11,780/t; FCX PLUNGES 7%, Comex 21% Below September Record
snippet: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell as much as 5.7% to approximately $11,780 per tonne — the biggest one-day drop in 19 months — as AI-spending doubts, a strengthening dollar, and weaker Chinese data combined to erase Monday's modest recovery. COMEX copper now sits 21% below its September 2026 record, technically placing it in bear market territory, while Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) fell 7% and Southern Copper (NYSE: SCCO) dropped 5% on the same session. For junior copper explorers and developers on the TSX-V and ASX, the selloff raises financing risk at exactly the stage when several companies were planning resource-stage raises ahead of year-end.

headline: GOLD BREAKS $3,600 FLOOR, SILVER SLIDES 5% — Rate Hike Bets Deepen November Rout Before Wednesday PCE Print
snippet: Spot gold fell below $3,600 per ounce and silver dropped as much as 5% to approximately $41.43 during Tuesday's North American session, as markets priced in a 95% probability of a December Federal Reserve rate hike ahead of Wednesday's October PCE inflation release — the last major data point before the FOMC's December meeting. The gold-silver ratio widened to 85, reflecting silver's disproportionate sensitivity to rate expectations, while Kitco's technical analysis identifies $3,595 as the level bears must break to target the $3,500 floor. Bulls need gold to reclaim the $3,651-$3,674 zone to signal a credible recovery; a soft PCE print Wednesday is the near-term catalyst that could reset December hike expectations.

headline: RINCON RESOURCES HITS 21m @ 2.40 g/t Au AND 3.83% Cu AT TELFER SOUTH — New Zone Extends 150m+; 10km from Greatland's Producing Telfer Operations
snippet: Rincon Resources (ASX: RCR) reported that drill hole HRC26011 at the Telfer South project in Western Australia returned 21 metres at 2.40 g/t gold and 3.83% copper from surface — confirming a new copper-gold zone at the northern end of the Hasties SE deposit, with mineralisation interpreted to extend more than 150 metres along strike and open in both directions at depth. The project sits approximately 10 kilometres from Greatland Resources' producing Telfer gold-copper operations, one of Australia's largest gold mines, providing an immediately relevant benchmark for grade and infrastructure. Assays are still pending for the remaining holes in the 2026 program, suggesting this result may not be the best intercept in the batch.

headline: USFM SIGNS TERM SHEET FOR 85% OF HOOK LAKE, NUNAVUT — Fully Permitted Gold-Copper Project; Footprint Expands in Arctic Canada
snippet: USFM signed a non-binding term sheet with Manhattan Gold Corporation (ASX: MHC) to acquire up to an 85% interest in the Hook Lake project in Nunavut, Canada — a fully permitted gold and copper exploration project in the Arctic. Full permitting for a Nunavut project is a meaningful value-protection feature given increasingly long Canadian permitting timelines, and the deal structure gives USFM operational control of a shovel-ready asset. The acquisition also sits in the context of USFM's pending merger with Twin Vee PowerCats, suggesting the company is building a portfolio of permitted assets ahead of that transaction.

headline: COPPER'S WORST MONTH IN YEARS HITS PERU TWICE — Output Fell 9% in September as AI Selloff Now Collapses Export Revenue
snippet: Copper's worst month in years is hitting Peru from two compounding directions: domestic mine output dropped 9% in September while the AI-driven November price collapse has now erased more than 20% of copper's September record, wiping a simultaneous hole in export revenues and government royalty receipts. Peru is the world's second-largest copper producer, and its fiscal position is unusually leveraged to copper prices, meaning the AI selloff and reduced tariff expectations translate directly into government budget pressure beyond the equity market impact visible in North American markets. For TSX-V investors evaluating copper-exposed juniors, the Peru data is a leading indicator of reduced appetite for South American acquisitions from the major producers that drive junior M&A activity.

headline: PRECIOUS METALS SELLOFF: FORCED SELLING OR REAL DEMAND RETREAT? — Silver Hit 7x Harder Than Gold; Analysts Flag Positioning Shock
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis of the precious metals selloff finds the evidence consistent with a technical positioning shock rather than a fundamental demand retreat: forced liquidation and margin calls are driving silver to fall at roughly seven times the percentage rate of gold — a spread that historical analysis says typically reverses sharply once positioning normalises. The piece notes that physical gold demand from central banks and Asian retail buyers has held at mid-year levels through November, arguing that a capitulation move driven by paper markets creates asymmetric risk for patient accumulators. Distinguishing positioning-driven selloffs from demand-driven bear markets is the key analytical question for retail investors deciding whether to add to mining positions during the November rout.

headline: SILVER FACES $43 CEILING ENTERING PCE WEEK — Gold-Silver Ratio at 85 as Market Prices 95% December Fed Hike
snippet: FXStreet's November 23 silver price forecast identifies $43 as the key resistance level heading into PCE week — a price silver must reclaim to stabilise the gold-silver ratio near 85, which currently sits at a level historically consistent with either a severe recession or a major positioning imbalance. With markets pricing a 95% chance of a December Fed rate hike, silver faces structural headwinds from both its industrial and monetary components simultaneously — an unusually unfavourable macro alignment that has historically preceded sharp mean-reversion rallies once the catalyst resolves. A PCE print above expectations would likely extend losses toward $40; a cool print could reset December hike odds and trigger the technical rebound silver bulls are waiting for.

headline: PREMIER AMERICAN URANIUM WRAPS 2026 KAYCEE PROGRAM — 13 of 19 Final Holes Hit Uranium at West Diane; 83,085 ft Drilled in 99 Holes
snippet: Premier American Uranium (TSX-V: PUR) concluded its 2026 exploration drilling program at the Kaycee project in Wyoming with 99 conventional mud-rotary drillholes totalling 83,085 feet, reporting that 13 of the 19 final holes at the West Diane zone encountered uranium mineralisation including grades up to 0.181% eU₃O₈ over 5 feet. The Wyoming programme is specifically designed to convert the Kaycee deposit's historical resources into a modern NI 43-101-compliant estimate under US uranium pricing tailwinds that have pushed long-term contract prices to records above $98/lb. For TSX-V uranium investors, Kaycee represents a pure-play US production jurisdiction at a time when utilities are urgently seeking contracted non-Russian supply.
